title: Space-Entropy Lower Bounds for Random Sampling
summary: We prove fundamental space lower bounds for exact random sampling using an entropy source of i.i.d. uniform bits. A classic result from information theory shows that generating $n$ discrete random variables $X_1, \dots, X_n$ requires at least $H(X_1, \dots, X_n)$ input random bits on average, where $H$ is the Shannon entropy function. How much space must a random sampling algorithm use in order to approach this information-theoretically optimal entropy bound?
